title: Combinatorics and probabilities of Kingman coalescent trees: histories, shapes, topologies, root splits, Colless, and Sackin
abstract: This entry formalizes combinatorics and probabilities of trees under Kingman's coalescent, through its embedded jump chain, in which each pair of the k current lineages is the next to merge with probability 1/binomial(k, 2). A ranked labelled history on n leaves is a sequence of n − 1 merges starting from n singletons; there are n!(n − 1)!/2^(n−1) of them, and each has probability 2^(n−1)/(n!(n − 1)!). Ranked and unranked tree shapes are defined as classes of histories under relabelling of the leaves; their numbers satisfy André's recurrence for alternating permutations, shifted by one, and the Wedderburn–Etherington recurrence, respectively, with the cases n = 1 and n = 2. The probability of a labelled rooted binary topology T is 2^(n−1)/(n! ∏(|C| − 1)), the product running over the clades C of T with at least two leaves. The probability that the root splits the leaves into a given set A and its complement is 2/((n − 1) binomial(n, |A|)). The probability that a sample S of a population of N leaves has the population root as its most recent common ancestor is (|S| − 1)(N + 1)/((|S| + 1)(N − 1)), which tends to (n − 1)/(n + 1) for a sample of fixed size n as N tends to infinity. The expected Colless and Sackin indices are n H_{⌊n/2⌋} − 2⌊n/2⌋ and 2n(H_n − 1), where H_m is the m-th harmonic number. Finally, the process of roots of the forest histories is identified with the jump chain of Kingman's partition-valued coalescent, for one step and for t steps.
